full_judgment:
3. The parties went to trail on two issues : (1) Whether the plaintiffs were entitled to claim the plaint amount, and (2) Whether the defendants were entitled to set-off the amount claimed by them. On consideration of evidence, oral and documentary, the trial Judge held that plaintiffs succeeded in proving their claim on which there was no challenge, and refused the claim of set-off on the ground that the amount was not ascertained and the carrier was not made a party to the suit. He, however, found negligence on the part of plaintiffs. He decreed the suit with costs. 

 5. Against this judgment and the decree, plaintiff-appellants have obtained special ease. Two questions are involved in this appeal : (1) In view of the fact that to claim set off under Order VIII, Rule 6, the amount shall have to be an ascertained sum, could the claim of defendants unliquidated damages for the loss of bales be said to be an ascertained sum ? And (2) whether fur the determination of liability of appellants in respect of damages, the carrier is a necessary patty. 

 8. On a comparison of rival contentions, we find that the submission of Mr. Hafizullah has great force. Defendants no doubt claimed specified sum and paid full court-fee thereon. Plaintiffs under the Code, had an opportunity of filing additional plaint in reply, disputing the claim of set-off but did not take any steps. At the trial defendants led oral evidence in support of their claim made in the written statement. The averment was made by the second defendant, the proprietor of the first defendant. He was not cross-examined, nor any witness called by plaintiffs in rebuttal to this statement. Could it then be said that in this context, the amount claimed by defendants, has become an ascertained sum of money as contemplated in rule 6, Order VIII of the Code ? The rule says, that when set-off is claimed, the written statement shall he treated as a plaint. For defendants to get a decree on this claim of set off, the Court has to adjudicate, and defendants are to satisfy it that they, in fact, suffered loss claimed by them, and they are to establish it on evidence. It not divided that the contract of carriage between plaintiffs and defendants did not contain any clause stipulating any sum as liquidated damages. The amount claimed by defendants is unliquidated damages. There is a string of authorities holding, that unliquidated damages are not an ascertained sum of money within the meaning of rule 6 of Order VIII. To cite only a few of them : Edward Dalgleish Vs. Ramdin Singh Choudhury 14 C.W.N. 170, Diltor Koer Vs. Harkhoo Singh A.I.R. 1916 Patna 167, Har Parsad Vs. Firm Ram Sarup Radha A.I.R. 1924 Allahabad 872, Pir Baksh Vs. Rameshwar Nath A.I.R. 1929 Allahabad 52, Galstaun Vs. Radhakissen A.I.R. 1931 Calcutta 23, Bhikanarao Vs. Sridhar A.I.R. 1931 Nagpur 12.
